January 26, 34.

Dear Mr. Sarly,

I forward herewith for your information tabulated
statements relating to the arrest by the Municipal Police
of two communists named Zung Loh Sheng (陳樂成) alias
Nyien Ts Zung (嚴子呈) alias Woo Kyung Sieu (吳敬修)
and Tsang Ih Sing (張一新) alias Zung Fso (張孚) alias
Waung Yah Dah (汪亞達) at 11.10 a.m. January 12, 1934 at
No.170 Zae Foong Li (瑞丰里) East Kashing Road.

The accused appeared on remand before the Second
Branch of the Kiangsu High Court on January 20, 1934 and
were ordered to be handed over to the Chinese authorities.

A list of the communist literature seized is
attached.

Yours sincerely,
JR

Monsieur R. Sarly,
Chief of the Political Section,
French Police Headquarters.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

On the 18-1-34 the lawyer for the 2nd accused interviewed him in Kashing Road Station Detective Office. During the conversation the undersigned overheard the accused ask his lawyer if the Police had discovered a certain document concealed in one of the Communist books seized at 170 East Kashing Road on the 12-1-34. On hearing this the lawyer promptly warned his client not speak. Acting on this the undersigned carefully examined each book seized in the above raid with the result that between pages 30 and 31 of a Communist periodical entitled "Red Flag Weekly", issue No. 62 was found a Communist document written in ink entitled "Working Plans of the "Chung Wei" for the month of January". (Translator's note: The name Chung Wei most probably denotes "The Military Committee"). A full translation by the Special Branch is attached hereto

The discovery of this document in the home of the 1st accused, the existence of which was known to the 2nd accused definitely destroys the statements of both accused in which they allege they do not know each other and therefore forms a strong connecting link which proves their complicity.

This case will come before the Court again on the 20-1-34 when the Public Safety Bureau will make an application for their extradition.

调查记录。

1934年1月18日，第二被告的律师在嘉善路警局侦探办公室会见了他。在谈话期间，签署人无意中听到被告询问其律师，警方是否发现了1934年1月12日在嘉善路东170号缴获的某本共产主义书籍中藏匿的一份特定文件。听到这话，律师立即警告他的客户不要说话。据此，签署人仔细检查了上述突袭行动中缴获的每一本书，结果在一本名为《红旗周报》第62期的共产主义刊物第30页和第31页之间，发现了一份用墨水书写的共产主义文件，题为“‘中委’一月份工作计划”。（译者注：名称“中委”很可能指“军事委员会”）。随函附上特务科的完整译文。

在第一被告家中发现这份文件，而第二被告知晓其存在，这彻底推翻了两名被告声称互不相识的供词，因此构成了证明他们共谋的有力关联证据。

本案将于1934年1月20日再次开庭，届时公安局将申请引渡他们。

through Inspector Kuh Pao Hwa with the Public Safety Bureau
representatives who assisted in the arrest and prevailed upon
them to attend this office in order to furnish further
particulars regarding the antecedents of these two men and their
recent subversive activities.

Information supplied by Inspector Wong Wen Tsing (王文俊)
of the P.S.B., who visited Special Branch Headquarters during
the afternoon of January 15, was to the effect that the real
name of Zung Loh Tseng, the 1st accused, was Nyien Tsz Zung

Defence groups among ricsha coolies, hut-dwellers, peasants,
seamen etc, his duty being to organise and assist them in
making demonstrations and creating disturbances.

Tsang Ih Seng, (the 2nd accused, is alleged to be a member

Committee of the Chinese Communist Party whose true name is
Zung Foo (陳孚) alias Waung Yeh Dah (王子達). According to the
P.S.B. representatives he graduated at a medical school in
Tokyo. Arrested by the Japanese authorities together with fifteen
other students, he is said to have refused to admit his
complicity in spite of the application of the Third Degree.

The Soviet is the motherland of labourers and farmers.

The Red Army is the defender of the motherland of

The victory of the Red Army will mean the expansion

什么是苏维埃？

苏维埃是劳工和农民的祖国。它最初建立在俄国。目前，苏维埃区也在中国发展。

苏维埃中国包括湖北、湖南、福建、江西、广东和江西各省。现在已明确将四川省染红。

什么是红军？

红军是劳工和农民祖国的保卫者。它正在与资本家和地主作战。

为什么红军强大？

红军的胜利意味着苏维埃区的扩大，这将给农民和劳工的家庭带来幸福。在满洲，日本帝国主义者正在与由农民和劳工组成的部队作战。日本的这些农民和劳工的家庭从日本的胜利中得不到任何好处，他们的生活状况只会越来越糟。在红军中，官兵之间从未有过摩擦。红军的指挥官是从劳工和农民中选拔出来的。他们生活在一起，吃同样的食物，穿同样的衣服。红军得到农民和劳工的有力支持。这些就是红军强大的部分原因。

Mr T.Y.Chang :- These two accused were arrested at 11.10.am. on the 12.1.54 at the request of the Bureau Of Public Safety and on the authority of a Warrant issued from this Court. at No.170 East Kashing Road in an upstairs room. Police entered the room and arrested the 1st accused. A crowd had gathered below to watch the proceedings. The 2nd accused entered the alleyway with the intention of coming to the 1st accused's room. Eung Leh Sheng(陈芳成), age 39,
Wenchong Hsien, Kwangtung                      D.S. Jones
Nanking Rd. 5tn      Jan. 12, 1934              Clerk Z.O. Sung.

My name is Eung Leh Sheng (        ), age 39, I was born in
Wenchong Hsien(文昌 ). My father, who was a small farmer,
died about three years ago.

From the age of 7 to 9 years I attended a small private school
at my native village. After this I assisted my father to
run the farm and continued doing this until about two years ago,
when I became a barber. At first I was my own master and
rented a small shop, but as this was not very profitable, I closed
down and worked as a street barber on the side-walks of my home
town.

In October, 1933, a friend of mine named Foo Hung Kyang
(蒲洪泾) met me at my native place and when I told him how bad
business was with me advised me to seek a job in Shanghai.

Together with my friend, who works on a ship, I travelled
from Canton to Hongkong. On September 29, 1933 I embarked on
a steamship at Hongkong and came to Shanghai. My friend is
employed on this vessel, the name of which I do not know, as a
coolie. The ship arrived at Shanghai on October 3 and for about
a month I lived with this friend at the "Chang-Yin"(琼崖 )Guild,
which is somewhere in the Eastern District. During this time I
earned my living as a street barber.

I have been living at my present address, No. 170 East
Nanking Road since last December 16. The reason I took this
room in which I was arrested was because the rent there was less
than that which I was obliged to pay at the Guild.

I am not a Communist, neither do I belong to any political
party.

The books found under my pillow were brought two days ago by
page_data.zh:
陈芳成 (Eung Leh Sheng)，39岁，
广东文昌县                      D.S. Jones
南京路5号      1934年1月12日              书记员 Z.O. Sung.

我叫陈芳成 (        )，39岁，出生于文昌县。我的父亲是一名小农，约三年前去世。

7岁至9岁时，我在家乡的一所私塾读书。此后我协助父亲经营农场，一直持续到约两年前，当时我成为了一名理发师。起初我自己开店，租了一间小铺面，但因生意不佳，我便关门歇业，在家乡的街道上做流动理发师。

1933年10月，一位名叫蒲洪泾 (Foo Hung Kyang) 的朋友在我的家乡遇见了我，当我告诉他我的生意多么糟糕时，他建议我去上海找工作。

我和这位在船上工作的朋友一起，从广州前往香港。1933年9月29日，我在香港登上一艘轮船来到上海。我的朋友受雇于这艘船（船名我不清楚），担任苦力。船只于10月3日抵达上海，在大约一个月的时间里，我和这位朋友住在东区某处的“琼崖”会馆。在此期间，我靠做流动理发师维持生计。

自去年12月16日以来，我一直居住在现址南京东路170号。我租用被捕时所在的这个房间，是因为那里的租金比我必须在会馆支付的租金要低。

我不是共产党员，也不属于任何政党。

在我枕头下发现的书籍是两天前由

out without saying a word. At 11 a.m. to-day the same person
brought some more books to my room and put them on my suitcase,
whence they were removed by the Police. On this occasion he
asked me to look after them for him. He was in a great hurry
and I did not have an opportunity to ask him why he wanted me,
a stranger, to do him this favour. At the time After the
Police raid I saw this same man outside my room on the landing.
The reason I did not tell the detectives about it was because
I was not asked.

I did not open the window in my room in order to signal
to my friends that a raid was taking place, but simply to let
a little air into the room.

(Signed) Sung Leh Sheng.

Tsang Ih Sing (張新)
Ningpo                                      D.S.Watts.
Kashing Road          12/1/34/              Inter. T.L.Chang.

My name is Tsang Ih Sing (張新), alias Zang Foo (章孚)
alias Waung Yah Dah (汪学達) age 24, native of Ningpo, single,
unemployed. I was born in the 3rd year of the Ching Dynasty at
Ningpo. My father is a farmer, I have no brothers or sisters. When
I was 9 years old I entered the Feng Hwa Elementary School (奉化小
学) at Fenghwa studying for 4 years when I entered the elementary
middle school, Fenghwa. After 2 years here I went to the Tinghai
Higher Middle School (定海中学) Tinghai studying here for 3 years when
I graduated and returned to the Fenghwa Elementary School where
where I became a teacher occupying this post for one and a half
years. I then entered the China College, Woosung where I studied
law for 2 years but owing to financial stringency I returned to
Fenghwa where I became a teacher in the Elementary Middle School.
On the 5th or 6th of this month I wrote a letter to my friend
Chen Kyah San (秦嘉山) c/o The New China College, Rue Chapel
asking him if he could find a job for me. I received a reply on
the 10th of this month in which he invited me to come to Shanghai
to discuss the matter and to meet him at 9.30 a.m. 12/1/34 at
the corner of Szechuen Rd. and Ave. Rd.VII. If I failed to see
him here I was to meet him at the Dixwell Road Market at 11 a.m.
the same day (12/1/34). I therefore came to Shanghai from Fenghwa
on the "Sing-kaing-tien" arriving at the Sing-kiang-tien wharf,
Nantao at 5.30 a.m. this morning 12/1/34. I stayed on the boat
for a time and afterwards had breakfast in a foodshop on the
wharf until it was time to keep my appointment. After waiting on
the corner of Szechuen Rd. and Ave. Rd. VII for about half an
hour I went for a walk and eventually mounted a No.8 bus with
page_data.zh:
张新 (Tsang Ih Sing)
宁波                                      D.S.Watts.
卡辛路          1934年1月12日/              口译员 T.L.Chang.

我叫张新 (Tsang Ih Sing)，又名章孚 (Zang Foo)，又名汪学达 (Waung Yah Dah)，24岁，宁波人，未婚，无业。我出生于清朝第三年（注：原文如此，疑为笔误，应指民国或具体年份）的宁波。我的父亲是农民，我没有兄弟姐妹。9岁时，我进入奉化小学就读，学习了4年后进入奉化初级初中。在那里读了2年后，我去了定海中学，在那里学习了3年并毕业，随后回到奉化小学担任教师，任职一年半。之后我进入吴淞中国学院学习法律2年，但因经济拮据返回奉化，在初级初中担任教师。本月5日或6日，我写信给我的朋友秦嘉山 (Chen Kyah San)，地址转交霞飞路新中国学院，询问他能否为我找份工作。本月10日我收到回信，邀请我来上海商议此事，并于1934年1月12日上午9:30在四川路与爱多亚路七路口与他见面。如果我在那里没见到他，我应于同日（1934年1月12日）上午11点在狄思威路市场与他见面。因此，我从奉化乘坐“新江天”轮来到上海，于1934年1月12日凌晨5:30抵达南市新江天码头。我在船上待了一段时间，然后在码头的食品店吃早餐，直到赴约的时间。在四川路与爱多亚路七路口等了约半小时后，我四处走走，最终乘上了一辆8路公交车，打算

page_data.en:
Continuation

the intention of going to the Dixwell Road Market as arranged.
I alighted at Kashing Road Bridge and was walking along N. Kashing
Road when I was arrested by detectives.
The slip of paper I tried to conceal in my rectum on my
arrest was enclosed in the letter Chen Nyah San wrote to me
requesting me to come to Shanghai. He asked me to write an essay
on the subject contained on the paper. I did same because I
thought that it was against the law to be anti-Japanese.
I am not a Communist and am not an adherent of any party.
My hobby is studying old Chinese books. I do not know the man
arrested with me (Zang Woh Sheng).
This is my true statement.

Signed and Thumb printed by
Tsang Ih Sing.

我在被捕时试图藏入直肠的那张纸条，附在秦嘉山写给我要求我来上海的信中。他要求我就纸条上的主题写一篇文章。我照做了，因为我认为反日是违法的。
我不是共产党员，也不依附于任何党派。
我的爱好是研读中国古籍。我不认识与我一同被捕的人（张沃生 Zang Woh Sheng）。
这是我的真实陈述。

张新 签名并按手印。
